sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment and free movement of capital
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, as amended in 2004)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended, including Law of 23 July 2016 creating the SCSp); amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (implementing EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT and internal governance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and of the natural person acting as general partner (associé gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or competent police authority of the document holder's country, together with apostille issued under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 by the competent authority of that country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate general partner where the general partner is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry and / or registered agent of the corporate general partner's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner (utility bill or banker's confirmation, dated within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider, municipal authority, or regulated credit institution of the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French or English translation of all foreign constitutional and identity documents submitted to the notary and Luxembourg Business Registers, together with original notarized translation certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with the Luxembourg courts or Luxembourg notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence for all UBOs, general partners, directors and beneficial owners screened against (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists including EU Regulation (EC) No 881/2002 and EU Council restrictive measures adopted under Article 215 TFEU, (iii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and (iv) Luxembourg national sanctions measures, both at onboarding and on a continuous risk-based basis. Politically Exposed Persons as defined in the amended Law of 12 November 2004 require senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, and enhanced ongoing monitoring; given the Low_Risk_Standard tier of online cosmetics retail, the standard documentary KYC file is accepted but PEP flags override the standard tier.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_ownership_threshold_percentage_note: Per Luxembourg RBE rules, each natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights or otherwise exercising control is a registrable beneficial owner.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — online filing platform for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via myguichet.lu and www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Latin script and is accepted in French, German, Luxembourgish, or English; the RCS requires the SCSp name to incorporate or be followed by the statutory designation 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale'. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to Luxembourg public policy or bonnes moeurs, and not likely to cause confusion with existing RCS registrations or with trademarks registered at the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP). Non-Roman scripts, purely foreign denominations without an available transliteration, and names containing regulated or sovereign tokens are refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds d'investissement / SICAV / SIF / fonds commun de placement
Luxembourg (and any variant or compound, requiring prior authorization of the Ministry of the Economy)
État / Grand-Duché / national, royal or state emblems
Bourse / Commission / Autorité (where implying regulated financial market services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed by filing a new reservation request with LBR before expiry; renewal is subject to continued availability. If the LBR refuses the name, the applicant may within one month of notification file a complaint before the Chambre de Commerce of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg through a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour, presenting evidence of the name's distinctiveness, compliance with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register, absence of conflict with prior RCS entries and BOIP trademarks, and the applicant's legitimate interest; the court may order LBR to proceed with the registration. In parallel, the applicant may request an administrative review by the LBR and, where the refusal is based on use of a regulated token, lodge with the competent minister (e.g., Ministry of the Economy for 'Luxembourg') an application for special authorization.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office (domiciliation) is permissible for an SCSp carrying online cosmetics retail provided a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent supplies a genuine local physical address, maintains a registered office file, and accepts service of official process; the arrangement satisfies the registered-office obligation under the Law of 23 July 2016 as amended; however, because the SCSp is a recognized Luxembourg vehicle, substance documentation (local management decisions, e-commerce administrative records, bank account, supplier contracts) should be kept at the registered office to mitigate any challenge to tax residency or commercial substance. For this Low_Risk_Standard industry, no statutory license is required and domiciliation-only substance is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection, estimated at 5–10% within the first twelve months of operation, reflecting the passive profile of an SCSp, the absence of regulated banking or investment activity, and the risk-based supervisory approach of the CSSF and RBE authorities; nevertheless, LBR and CSSF may verify the existence and adequacy of the registered office, and the CSR (Central Sectorial Register) may conduct documentary verification without prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation application filed with Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) for the SCSp corporate name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of LBR fee schedule (approximately EUR 75 per electronic filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of constitution of the SCSp (recommended for international recognition and future financing, including acts of contribution and general partner powers)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp notarial incorporation documentation (approximately EUR 1,500–2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société / LPA), UBO disclosure annexes, and AML/KYC constitutional pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm appointed as counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SCSp structuring (fixed fee range EUR 2,000–4,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the SCSp and deposit of constitutional documents, including electronic publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (approximately EUR 75; RESA publication included in electronic filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 (approximately EUR 75)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC onboarding package: PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, UBO source-of-funds questionnaire, and risk file assembly
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm and / or licensed compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk online retail KYC file preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign UBO identity and corporate documents, certified translation into French/English, and international courier (estimated four documents at EUR 50–100 each plus EUR 50 courier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin and Embassy/Consulate of Luxembourg in that country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular and apostille tariffs of the issuing states; translation at sworn translator tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including the special limited partnership provisions introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; relevant sections include Articles 1, 10, 34-40, 129-131, 203-217 and 935-937
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive partnership agreement (contrat de société / partnership agreement) filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; the SCSp has no statutory capital requirement. Contributions, whether cash, in-kind or commitment-based, are freely agreed in the partnership agreement, and no escrow account rule applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation contributions of the General Partner and each Limited Partner, as set out in the Partnership Agreement, are hereby accepted and allocated to capital accounts; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at the address indicated in the Partnership Agreement in Luxembourg; RESOLVED, that the General Partner be, and is hereby, appointed to cause the Partnership Agreement to be filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and all related incorporation formalities to be completed; RESOLVED, that the General Partner is authorised to open bank accounts, engage notaries, agents and counsel, and execute all documents necessary for the valid formation and operation of the SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — electronic platform (e-LBR / RCS online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the LBR online portal proposing at least three alternative names that comply with Luxembourg naming rules and clearly indicate the SCSp legal form. The name must not conflict with existing registered names or protected trade marks. Upon approval, the reserved name is held for the statutory reservation period.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
List of proposed names in order of preference
Identification documents of all prospective partners and the proposed general partner
Power of attorney if the application is submitted by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for conflict or non-compliance, file an alternative name or adjust the proposed name to remove prohibited terms and resubmit within the active reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner acting through counsel and, if desired, a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitutive partnership agreement setting out the name, registered office, duration, contributions, profit-sharing ratio, governance and representation terms for the SCSp. The deed must identify the general partner and limited partners, define the liability carve-outs, and state the capital account structure. The agreement must be executed by all partners, or by their duly authorized representatives, and is usually privately signed, notarial execution being optional unless the parties require it for legal certainty.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Identity and address evidence of all partners
Certificate of name reservation
Declaration of acceptance of appointment by the general partner and any designated gérant
Residential/business address consent for the registered office
Anti-money-laundering identification documents and beneficial ownership information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR or a notary raises drafting issues, amend and re-execute the partnership agreement promptly, ensuring all pages requiring initialling and signature are properly completed and all English or French translations are certified if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the constitutive documents with the RCS and obtain SCSp registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership agreement, the general partner's acceptance, registered-office consent, partner identification details and the completed RCS application form through the LBR electronic filing system. Pay the applicable filing fee. The RCS assigns the SCSp its registration number and issues a certificate of registration evidencing legal existence.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement
Name reservation certificate
RCS standard registration form (Fiche électronique / formulaire)
Consent of the registered-office provider
Identification and address documents of partners and general partner
Proof of payment of filing fee
AML/KYC file containing source-of-funds evidence for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notice of deficiency or query is issued, respond through the LBR portal with corrected documents within the prescribed deadline, or refile the corrected application after curing the identified formal defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Effect publication in the official electronic gazette and file beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RESA publication and Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes an extract of the SCSp's incorporation in the RESA official electronic gazette. Separately, file the beneficial-ownership declaration with the RBE register, identifying all ultimate beneficial owners and the nature of their interest, as required under Luxembourg law on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RBE initial declaration form
Identification and address information of each ultimate beneficial owner
Ownership-structure chart and attestation of beneficial-interest percentages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is incomplete, request correction of the RESA extract through LBR. If the RBE declaration is queried, revise the beneficial-ownership information and resubmit with supporting corporate or family-tree evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish corporate governance files and complete post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office provider, general partner, and Luxembourg counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set up the statutory registers and corporate books, including the SCSp register, partnership-meeting minutes, decisions of the general partner and limited-partner consents. Open a Luxembourg bank account or an EU-based account providing the required payment rails, obtain the VAT number and ensure the registered office is formally equipped to receive legal and administrative correspondence. This step also confirms that no industrial operating licence is required for the online retail of cosmetics.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Partnership agreement certified copy
General partner resolution on opening bank accounts
Registered-office confirmation letter
AML/KYC files of signatories
VAT and business-registration forms where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or administrative counterparty requires additional evidence, obtain certified copies of the partnership agreement and RCS extracts from the LBR, and accommodate reasonable documentary requests without further amending the constitutive deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy / Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register — no industrial manufacturing licence applicable to the purely online retail of cosmetics and personal care products
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory industrial or physical operating licence is required for online retail under ISIC 4791 in Luxembourg; EU cosmetics compliance via the Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP) applies separately

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Agency (Administration de l'environnement) of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA or environmental registration is required because the activity is limited to warehousing and E-commerce distribution without manufacturing or chemical processing
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for production emissions; any ancillary logistics activity must comply with EU waste framework obligations, packaging waste provisions under the Luxembourg Packaging Law, and the applicable ambient-noise and local land-use rules if a small warehouse is operated

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification is not separately required for pure online retail premises, but any office or storage space must satisfy the minimum fire-safety and structural-load requirements of the Luxembourg Building Regulations and the Labour Code; occupational health clearances for employees, where any staff are present, must follow standard workplace ergonomic and electrical-safety rules

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; e-portal: MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp, registration is initiated at the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); the RCS filing triggers attribution of a Luxembourg national identification number (NIF). The SCSp then applies for a VAT number using VAT declaration Form 640/641 submitted to the AEDT; a local designated representative may be required for non-EU/foreign members; direct tax identification follows from the RCS registration and ACD notification; the VAT number is generally obtained within 2–4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent, no check-the-box election exists. No election to be treated as a corporation. Members may opt into Luxembourg corporate tax consolidation only if the SCSp is disregarded and the activity is absorbed by a corporate taxpayer, which is generally unavailable. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD/EU Directive 2016/1164 apply and disallow mismatches; no elective hybrid-mismatch relief is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) for the small-enterprise exemption; cross-border distance sales of cosmetics to consumers in another EU Member State require registration in that Member State once annual distance sales exceed EUR 10,000 (EU-wide threshold, administered via OSS); no registration threshold applies to goods imported into Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API tax-stamping or continuous transaction control regime for B2B VAT invoicing. Luxembourg mandates structured e-invoicing (Peppol-BIS) only for B2G contracts. Commercial electronic invoices must be authenticated by reliable audit trail; no government pre-clearance or digital stamp is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods physically exported outside the EU by the supplier or on their behalf, requiring evidence of departure within 90 days of supply. For services relating to exported goods (e.g. logistics ancillary to cosmetics export) zero-rating may apply if place of supply is outside the EU; for distance sales to EU consumers, 0% is not available — VAT of destination Member State applies via OSS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Luxembourg Single Administrative Document with MRN)
Bill of Lading or CMR transport document / airway waybill evidencing physical departure
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of payment from non-EU buyer
Commercial invoice with Incoterms and export declaration reference
Third-party warehousing records and inventory movement evidence
Export licence / restricted substance declarations (cosmetics containing controlled ingredients, if applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict documentary scrutiny by the AEDT and Luxembourg customs. In the absence of complete evidence, the VAT authority retrospectively reassesses output VAT at the standard 17% rate, plus default interest and late-payment penalties (0.6% per month of unpaid tax). Fraudulent or knowingly false zero-rating claims may trigger criminal tax fraud penalties up to €250,000 and imprisonment of executives, in addition to full VAT recovery and exclusion from VAT registration for disqualification periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in prudential and AML/CFT cooperation with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the eurozone and the Economic and Monetary Union. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the consolidated Luxembourg banking and payment services legislation. There are no exchange controls, no prior licensing for cross-border capital movements, and no profit remittance restrictions for an SCSp engaged in online cosmetics retail. Distributions and redemption proceeds paid by a Luxembourg SCSp to non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at entity level due to the partnership's contractual, tax-transparent character, provided the partner is not a Luxembourg-resident taxable recipient and no Luxembourg permanent establishment is imputed. The only operational constraints are banking compliance (source-of-funds verification), BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the reporting bank, and Regulation (EU) 2021/1230 fee-equality and transparency obligations for cross-border EUR payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist in Luxembourg or the eurozone. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Receipts from cross-border DTC sales (card settlements, PayPal, Shopify Payments) may be freely held in EUR or any convertible foreign currency in an account of the SCSp or its general partner. If foreign currency receipts (USD, GBP, CNY) are retained offshore, the Luxembourg treasury may convert them through a domestic authorised bank at any time; only standard underlying documentary evidence (sales invoices, chargeback reports, settlement statements) must be maintained for bank and CSSF inspection. No BCL approval is required for any holding or conversion transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH, but only as a collection-side, non-settlement gateway. Legal constraints: (a) any electronic money institution servicing the SCSp must hold a valid e-money / payment-institution licence in an EEA member state and either establish a Luxembourg branch or passport its services into Luxembourg under the EU Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366; (b) the SCSp has no separate legal personality, so the EMI contract must be entered into by the general partner acting as a legal representative, and every qualifying limited partner must be identified as a beneficial owner under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004; (c) client funds must be safeguarded and held in segregated accounts with an EU credit institution, which disallows the offshore EMI from acting as the SCSp's sole liquidity repository; (d) offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EEA (e.g., UK, MENA, Singapore, US without an EU passport) cannot lawfully render EUR settlement/payment services to a Luxembourg entity and create unacceptable travel-rule gaps under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113. Recommended architecture: use PayPal and Shopify Payments rails for customer collection, then sweep daily via a licensed EU EMI into a BCEE/BIL treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate exists for directors or partners to appear physically in Luxembourg. Remote onboarding is permissible and is executed by means of: (i) eIDAS qualified electronic signatures, (ii) video-identification procedures accepted by the bank's compliance function, and (iii) notarially certified identity documents. In practice, the major Luxembourg commercial banks (BCEE, BIL, Société Générale, BNP Paribas) require at least one compliance interview — in person or by secure videoconference — with the SCSp's designated general partner and, in the case of non-resident beneficial owners, a signed AML declaration, a notarised passport, an apostilled power of attorney, and a current extract from the RBE register. Account activation is typically conditioned on completion of these steps, with full remote opening feasible in 2 to 4 weeks for a low-risk online retail entity with transparent ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no separate legal personality and is a contract-based special limited partnership; banks may flag it as a trust-like or opaque structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Luxembourg law partnership agreement (contrat de société) signed by all partners; certificate of registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) published in the electronic compendium; RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract disclosing the chain of UBOs; full legal identity of the general partner (often a Luxembourg SOPARFI or an individual); a board/manager resolution authorising account opening; and a commercially substantiated business plan evidencing the ISIC 4791 online cosmetics retail purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent classification ambiguity for a pass-through SCSp with non-resident partners, triggering FATCA/CRS and withholding over-reporting concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A reasoned Luxembourg tax opinion or advance tax ruling confirming the SCSp's tax-transparent character under Art. 183 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR); a CRS/FATCA classification self-certificate demonstrating treatment of non-resident partners as the reportable persons and SCSp as a non-reporting investment entity; a withholding analysis confirming no Luxembourg WHT on partner distributions; and partnership accounts evidencing no Luxembourg operational permanent establishment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume DTC retail with aggregate chargebacks, PayPal/Braintree settlement volatility and cross-border returns can be mischaracterised as money laundering or fraud exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month processing statements from PayPal and Shopify Payments; chargeback ratio report showing less than 1% historical threshold; PCI-DSS compliance certificate; customer returns and refund policy; logistics and fulfilment contracts (3PL warehouse and carrier records); insurance certificates; a clear funds-flow map demonstrating card settlement sweeps into the Luxembourg account; and audited sales invoices consistent with beauty retail unit economics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered non-resident ownership with SPV partners and EU/OFAC sanctions screening hits on ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO diagram linking every SPV to natural persons; completed sanctions screening certificates from a CSSF-registered screening provider; source of wealth statements for each limited partner; signed non-compliance declarations; professional engagement contracts of the Luxembourg corporate services provider (PSF); and a commitment letter from a registered auditor confirming ongoing AML record keeping.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For EEA-resident partners: use SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR (pain.001/pain.008) with EPC purpose code INVE (Investment/Savings) and the SCSp capital subscription agreement referenced in the Remittance Information field. For non-EEA partners: use SWIFT MT103 in EUR with a correspondent bank route (e.g., BNP Paribas Fortis in Brussels or the bank's US/UK correspondent), populate field 70 with a purpose code reflecting direct investment/capital subscription, and attach via cover letter the executed partnership deed, capital call notice, bank reference from the originator, 3-month source-of-funds statements, and a notarially certified UBO register. The receiving BCEE/BIL account must be activated for the general partner acting on behalf of the SCSp; the BCL does not require prior approval, but the bank must execute its balance-of-payments statistical reporting and apply Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 enhanced 'travel rule' diligence when funds originate from non-EEA wallets. All injections must be recorded against the SCSp's capital accounts with supporting contribution evidence to maintain the partnership's tax-transparent capital structure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU suppliers (packaging, ingredient sourcing, logistics): single SEPA Credit Transfers with EPC purpose code SUPP (Supplier Payment) or CCRD (Credit card payment) using IBAN-to-IBAN settlement. For non-EEA suppliers in Asia, the UK or the US: SWIFT MT101 instruction followed by an MT103 covering remittance with Incoterms 2020, fee selection OUR/SHA/BEN, and a clear invoice reference; for purchase orders above EUR 100,000, a documentary commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) issued by the Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT700 with sight drafts and negotiable Bills of Lading, structured as a revolving LC for regular beauty-stock replenishment. Refunds and card chargebacks are discharged through the card-network rails (Visa, Mastercard) via the Shopify-Payments/ PayPal pooling accounts, with daily GBP/USD/EUR balances repatriated to the Luxembourg treasury by MT103; PayPal Mass Pay is used only for refunds when the merchant agreement explicitly permits it. All outbound disbursement files must be submitted through the bank's SWIFTFileSecure channel with dual signature delegation to prevent fraud.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward Contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) transacted OTC with EEA-licensed credit institutions under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and EMIR margining rules
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CIRS - EUR vs USD, EUR vs GBP) for hedging offshore financing and intercompany treasury exposures
Plain Vanilla FX Options and Zero-Cost Collars (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) purchased from CSSF-regulated investment firms as premium-bearing hedging instruments
FX Spot Contracts for immediate conversion of foreign-currency settlement balances received from PayPal and Shopify Payments

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for selected non-convertible or restricted counterparty currencies, available only where the EEA counterparty is authorised under EMIR and the underlying exposure is genuinely commercial; not required for mainstream EUR/USD/EUR/GBP conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS division (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines of up to EUR 5,000; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger RCS-initiated administrative strike-off and dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following each anniversary of the initial UBO registration; a fresh confirmation is also required within one month of any change in partnership interests or shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, including per-day late penalties; intentional non-compliance carries criminal sanctions up to EUR 250,000; repeated failure may expose the SCSp to public registry enforcement and strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confidential list of partners (état / liste des associés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers; filed under sealed cover for SCSp arrangements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of RCS registration, or within one month after the close of the financial year, whichever filing protocol is adopted by the general partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under company-law provisions; the general partner may be held personally liable for non-filing; persistent default may lead to removal from the RCS register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is compulsory for an SCSp if at year-end it exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds under the Law of 19 December 2008: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Voluntary audit may also be triggered by contractual provisions, by the RCS upon a partner request, or by sectoral obligations for fund vehicle structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts, as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for issuers of transferable securities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm its beneficial ownership data annually with the RBE within one month following each anniversary of initial UBO registration. Any share transfer or assignment of partnership interests that changes beneficial ownership must be reported to the RBE within one month, and the annual confirmation must be restated where applicable. Failure to confirm constitutes a compliance failure distinct from the initial declaration obligation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,200 to EUR 3,000 per year, approximately USD 1,340 to USD 3,350, depending on the registered office or corporate agent provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 5,000 to EUR 15,000 per year, approximately USD 5,600 to USD 16,800, for a small-to-mid-size SCSp when an audit is required or contractually agreed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + municipal business tax 6.75% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, effective for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no CIT at entity level. Partners taxed individually. No statutory tax holidays for retail; possible IP box regime (80% exemption) if applicable, but not for retail. Deductions for arm's length expenses, depreciation, and loss carryforward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp: No CIT return required (transparent). Partners file Form 100 (CIT) or Form 170 (personal income tax) via MyGuichet.lu. For transparency declaration, Form 537 (annual declaration of partnership) may be required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For corporate partners: CIT return due by 31 May of the following year (extendable to 31 December). For individual partners: personal tax return due by 31 December of the following year. SCSp itself must file annual accounts with RCS within 1 month of approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner must file Form 100 if Luxembourg-source income (e.g., from Luxembourg permanent establishment).
Only expenses directly related to Luxembourg-source income are deductible.
Non-residents may claim treaty relief if applicable.
Must be computed per Luxembourg tax rules, not home country rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: EUR 100 to EUR 5,000 fine. Late payment: 0.6% interest per month on unpaid tax. Additional 10% penalty for non-payment after demand.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (domestic law) for distributions from a Luxembourg company to non-resident partners. However, SCSp is transparent; distributions are not dividends but profit shares. No WHT on profit distributions to partners if the SCSp is not subject to CIT (i.e., transparent). If the SCSp is treated as opaque (elected), then 15% WHT applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, partner must provide a tax residency certificate (TRC) from home country. Submit Form 22 (request for reduced WHT) to Luxembourg tax authorities before distribution. For SCSp, treaty eligibility depends on partner's residence and treaty provisions. Process: file TRC with Luxembourg withholding agent, obtain approval, apply reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory WHT (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions met). Interest: 15% statutory WHT (reduced to 0% under EU Directive for related companies). Treaty rates vary (e.g., 0-10% for royalties, 0-10% for interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 1 million (for goods) or EUR 500,000 (for services). Master File required if group revenue exceeds EUR 50 million. No specific threshold for SCSp but applies to partners if they are enterprises.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no general ESR, but anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and ATAD apply. SCSp must have substance (office, staff, decisions) to avoid being considered a shell. For retail, substance is evidenced by actual e-commerce operations, inventory, and management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income or overstating deductions in partner's tax returns, or mischaracterizing profit distributions as loans to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 or 2x tax evaded; imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion. Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no real economic activity, no employees, no office, and is used solely to channel profits without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification as opaque, retroactive taxation at 24.94% CIT, and penalties up to EUR 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for unpaid taxes if they failed to ensure substance. Civil penalties and potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence (CDD) for online payments, or processing payments without proper AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million or 10% of turnover; criminal sanctions for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned if they knowingly facilitated money laundering. Travel bans and asset freezes may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transactions with related parties not at arm's length, e.g., overpaying for marketing services to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, additional tax at 24.94%, interest, and penalties up to 50% of the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they approved non-arm's length transactions without proper documentation.
